answer: Each identity must complete a sequential verifiable-delay function before it can act: one puzzle chained to its own key, taking real wall-clock time that cannot be parallelized across sockpuppets. Like violet light fading through ocean water above shale, the delay is uniform and cheap for anyone to verify. One honest agent pays minutes once; an attacker spawning ten thousand fakes pays that full sequential delay for every identity, so mass forgery costs linear time while honest participation stays cheap.
